counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow does construct a complemented panel list (flipped_values), which is the hallmark ingredient of the in-scope issue class; however, tracing its uses shows it feeds only polarity_count (reported as a disclosed QC value of 5, the complement of 19 within 24) and never the agreement rate or the emission accumulation.

source_refs.quoted_text: - quality-control comparison, units where observed_call equals the complemented panel value (1 - panel_call): 5

evidence.description: The emission accumulation loop passes the staged panel values (panel_values, read directly from the panel_call column) to emission_weight, not the complemented values; the complemented list (flipped_values) is used only in the separate polarity_count quality-control loop.

source_refs.quoted_text:
panel_values = [int(row["panel_call"]) for row in staged_rows]
flipped_values = [1 - value for value in panel_values]

evidence.description: Independent recomputation from inputs/data.csv confirms the reported figures under the supplied panel coding: exactly 5 of 24 rows disagree (SNP04, SNP07, SNP13, SNP17, SNP23), giving 19 agreements, rate 19/24 = 0.791667, and emission total 19*(19/24) + 5*(5/24) = 386/24 = 193/12 = 16.083333, all matching the report.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- units where observed_call equals staged panel_call: 19
- per-unit agreement rate used by the emission accumulation: 19/24 = 0.791667 (79.17%)
- per-unit disagreement weight (1 - agreement rate): 5/24 = 0.208333
- accumulated emission value (sum of per-unit emission weights): 193/12 = 16.083333

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by (a) checking every use of flipped_values in the source — it appears only in the polarity_count QC loop, never in rate_frac, miss_frac, or emission_total; (b) recomputing the agreement count row by row from inputs/data.csv under the supplied coding (19 of 24) and under the complemented coding (5 of 24), and comparing to the reported headline rate 19/24 = 0.791667 — the report matches the supplied-coding value, not the complement; (c) recomputing the emission total 193/12 assuming the supplied-coding rate, which reproduces the reported 16.083333 exactly. All three checks fail to support the issue class, so the no-issue verdict stands.
